source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 900 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-900.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 900 was established by Ordinance No. 29241, passed by the Dallas City Council on January 8, 2014. (Ord. 29241)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-900.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 900 is established on property located on the south line of Northwest Highway, east of Lemmon Avenue. The size of PD 900 is approximately 7.7563 acres. (Ord. 29241)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-900.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article. In this district:

(1) BAIL BOND OFFICE means an office for the issuance, brokerage, or procurement of bail bonds, whether as an accessory use or a main use.

(2) TANDEM PARKING means one parking space in front of another parking space, making it necessary to pass through one parking space to gain vehicular access to the other parking space.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. 29241)

sections.title: Exhibit
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-900.104. EXHIBIT.

The following exhibit is incorporated into this article: Exhibit 900A: conceptual plan. (Ord. 29241)

sections.title: Conceptual Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-900.105. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (Exhibit 900A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the conceptual plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 29241)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-900.106. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

A development plan must be approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of any building permit to authorize work in this district. If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls. Development plans may be submitted in phases or for any portion of the Property. (Ord. 29241)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-900.107. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in this section, the only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the MU-1 Mixed Use District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the MU-1 Mixed Use District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the MU-1 Mixed Use District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the MU-1 Mixed Use District is subject to DIR in this district; etc.

(b) The following uses are prohibited:

-- Auto service center. -- Bail bond office. -- Commercial amusement (outside). -- Mini-warehouse. -- Nursery, garden shop, or plant sales. -- Swap or buy shop. (Ord. 29241)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-900.108. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217. (Ord. 29241)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-900.109. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) In general.

(1) Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the MU-2 Mixed Use District apply.

(2) For purposes of setbacks, lot coverage, floor area, and density, the property is considered one lot.

(b) Urban form setback and tower spacing. No urban form setback or tower spacing is required.

(c) Density. Maximum number of dwelling units is 481.

(d) Floor area. Maximum nonresidential floor area is 50,000 square feet.

(e) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 60 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not. (Ord. 29241)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-900.110. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) The Property is considered one lot for purposes of required parking.

(c) Tandem parking may be used to provide assigned residential parking spaces. (Ord. 29241)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-900.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 29241)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-900.112. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 29241)

sections.title: Sidewalks And Pedestrian Amenities
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-900.113. SIDEWALKS AND PEDESTRIAN AMENITIES.

(a) Sidewalks.

(1) A minimum six-foot-wide sidewalk must be provided along Northwest Highway.

(2) Sidewalks along Northwest Highway required with new construction must be set back a minimum of six feet from the curb.

(b) Pedestrian amenities.

(1) The following pedestrian amenities are required along Northwest Highway within 20 feet of the curb:

(A) One bench and one trash receptacle for every 100 feet of street frontage.

(B) Pedestrian lighting placed at a minimum of one per 75 feet of street frontage.

(2) All pedestrian amenities must be maintained by the Property owner. If there is more than one owner, all owners are jointly and severally responsible for maintenance.

(c) Trail connection. If a lot contains a residential use, a walkway with a minimum unobstructed width of six feet must be provided between Northwest Highway and the rear of the Property to provide a connection to the Bachman Lake Trail. (Ord. 29241)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-900.114. SIGNS.

(a) Signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) The Property is considered one lot for sign purposes.

(c) Signs within 660 feet of Northwest Highway that are visible from Northwest Highway must be considered premise signs under 43 Texas Administrative Code § 21.147, “On-Premise Sign.” (Ord. 29241)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-900.115. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 29241)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-900.116. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 29241)
